It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the sufficiency of God’s Word and the danger of “itching ears” in this hour? [13, 1406, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock” by teaching “smooth things” to please the world, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory that needs no supplement? [1, 13, 20, 437, 730, 853, 1143, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with the culture, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by demanding that we “rightly divide the word of truth” [11, 28, 871, 1503, 1515, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the availability of His Word is not an “administrative anomaly” but a “lavish endowment” meant to provide “repose of the soul” and “total truth” for every believer [15, 68, 1323, 1339, 1445, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The All-Sufficient Standard for Guidance**

**Verse**
“All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work” (2 Timothy 3:16–17). [859, 1062, 1331, Conversation History]. “The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple; the statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes” (Psalm 19:7–8). [860, 1330, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that Scripture is “God-breathed” and therefore “wholly sufficient” to direct the life of the believer [711, 859, 1312, 1331, Conversation History]. Because the Bible is the “inspired Word of Almighty God,” it provides the “binding and authoritative mandate” for all conduct, meaning it does not need to be “supplemented or reduced” by human ingenuity or “modern drivel” [861, 890, 1312, 1333, Conversation History]. This “more sure word of prophecy” is the “traveler’s map” and the “soldier’s sword,” proving that “all things that pertain to life and godliness” are already contained within the “Spirit-inspired Scriptures” (2 Peter 1:3; 1:19) [595, 765, 785, 1151, 1328, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge,” for the Bible is the “only source of divine revelation and power” that can sustain you in your “daily walk with God” (James 1:17; Psalm 119:105) [51, 123, 1333, 1334, 1503, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word,” for “the Word of our God stands forever” while human “psychology and philosophy” vanish like smoke (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2; Isaiah 40:8) [11, 121, 251, 858, 1306, 1381, 1503, 1684, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” were often “punctilious” about “rabbinic tradition” and “legal minutiae,” yet they “neglected the weightier matters” and “corrupted the good things God had taught” (Matthew 23:23) [8, 14, 176, 248, 1053, 1352, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, showing that we are no longer bound by “ritualized ceremonies” but by a “mind transformed by the renewing of biblical truth,” for “the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands” (Romans 12:2; Acts 7:48) [13, 24, 142, 876, 1042, 1313, 1426, 1445, 1529, 1646, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Warning Against "Itching Ears"**

**Verse**
“For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but according to their own desires, because they have itching ears, they will heap up for themselves teachers; and they will turn their ears away from the truth, and be turned aside to fables” (2 Timothy 4:3–4). [258, 1461, 1530, Conversation History]. “ ‘An astonishing and horrible thing has been committed in the land: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own power; and My people love to have it so’ ” (Jeremiah 5:30–31). [731, 1516, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals a recurring “human tendency” to “seek to be enlightened” by “cleverly devised myths” that satisfy “sinful desires” rather than the “spotless purity of truth” [4, 28, 439, 1307, 1359, 1391, 1500, 1532, Conversation History]. Those with “itching ears” seek “spiritual placebos” from “spiritual swindlers” who “pander for publicity” and “market miracles” to suit a “consumer-driven culture” [32, 410, 421, 477, 672, 1616, Conversation History]. These “blind guides” offer “smooth things” and “deceits” because “men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil” (Isaiah 30:10; John 3:19) [11, 730, 1131, 1405, 1460, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “discipline your mind” to “examine everything carefully,” refusing to follow “apostate leaders” who “cater to people’s itching ears” for the sake of “dishonest gain” (1 Thessalonians 5:21; Titus 1:11) [33, 90, 116, 138, 294, 521, 1313, 1371, 1406, 1453, 1484, 1515, 1709, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” for though “the love of many will grow cold” and many follow “destructive ways,” the “Master and Owner” of the church will “preserve the gospel” for His own (Matthew 24:12; 2 Peter 2:2) [11, 21, 94, 201, 764, 808, 1143, 1408, 1492, 1500, 1515, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Jurisdiction**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “false prophecy” was a “capital offense” because it “counseled rebellion against the LORD” and sought to “seduce” the people from the path of life (Deuteronomy 13:5) [95, 554, 728, 904, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the “warfare,” teaching that while we “do not war according to the flesh,” we must “contend earnestly for the faith” using the “sword of the Spirit” to “cast down arguments” that “deny the only Lord God” (Jude 3; 2 Corinthians 10:4–5; Jude 4) [43, 92, 113, 201, 723, 1102, 1109, 1313, 1325, 1408, 1415, 1440, 1479, 1515, 1520, 1601, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Sufficiency of the Written Word**

**Verse**
“ ‘Abraham said to him, “They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” And he said, “No, father Abraham; but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.” But he said to him, “If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead” ’ ” (Luke 16:29–31). [279, 281, 283, Conversation History]. “ ‘For I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book’ ” (Revelation 22:18). [1324, 1331, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles the “clamor and kegiatan” of those seeking “fresh revelation” by affirming that “there is no need of further truth” because the “canon of the New Testament” is closed [121, 123, 124, 316, 568, 574, 1326, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—upheld by **John Calvin**—warns that “whatever does not have its origin in the Scriptures is surely from the devil himself,” for “the Word of God is not chained” and provides “the truth once for all delivered” (2 Timothy 2:9; Jude 3) [25, 41, 123, 735, 783, 1137, 1325, 1420, 1467, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History]. Relying on “impressions,” “visions,” or “psychic intuition” is a “spirit of fraud” that “undermines the authority of Scripture” and “competes with the exclusivity of biblical revelation” [11, 122, 186, 317, 343, 345, 348, 598, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by those who “label human intuition as divine prophecy,” for “your life is not your own” and you must instead “be filled with the Word” to “guard the faith” (1 Corinthians 6:20; 1 Timothy 6:20) [12, 91, 101, 347, 697, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1411, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. “Saturate and renew your mind” with the “more sure word of testimony,” for “faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God” (Romans 10:17; 2 Peter 1:19) [11, 21, 101, 116, 282, 764, 785, 855, 1334, 1406, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “divination and soothsaying” were “abominations” because they involved “demonic activity” that caricatured the Lord’s will (Deuteronomy 18:10) [888, 1160, 1346, 1428, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “witness,” revealing that the Spirit’s work is primarily “illumination” to understand the “Spirit-inspired Scriptures” rather than “new revelation,” for the “word of Christ” must “dwell in you richly” (Colossians 3:16; 1 Corinthians 2:12) [13, 125, 485, 573, 761, 795, 835, 1336, 1409, 1494, 1503, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Verdict on False Teaching**

**Verse**
“ ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’ ” (Matthew 7:23). [276, 318, 331, 1487, 1534, Conversation History]. “ ‘God has numbered your kingdom and put an end to it.… You have been weighed on the scales and found deficient’ ” (Daniel 5:26–27). [38, 1061, 1402, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of “destructive heresies” by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 16, 20, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1311, 1315, 1500, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. Those who “practice lawlessness” (*anomia*) by living “as though He never gave a law to obey” will be “crushed under divine judgment,” for the Lord “is against the prophets who envision futility” (Jeremiah 23:31) [11, 256, 331, 732, 733, 1058, 1396, 1461, 1506, 1512, 1720, Conversation History]. All “human monuments” and “building enterprises” of false doctrine will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away,” but the “Word of our God stands forever” (Isaiah 40:8; Psalm 102:3) [11, 32, 35, 37, 63, 789, 976, 1233, 1306, 1460, 1684, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “perfect justice will come” from the “Lord, the righteous Judge” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Timothy 4:8) [11, 14, 24, 94, 109, 201, 267, 351, 852, 948, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the “surest foundation,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” and the “final honoring of Jesus Christ” is “secure” (Daniel 7:14; 2 Timothy 2:19) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 211, 352, 412, 602, 630, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 201, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

If you don’t get an immediate answer to your request, or if events don’t turn out exactly or as quickly as you hoped they would, our Lord’s word to us is, “Don’t lose heart.” Just keep praying without ceasing and don’t give up. Keep knocking. Keep asking. Keep seeking. Spurgeon offered this insight to the importance of our persistence:

Let’s look at a specific example from the book of Job. In the midst of terrible suffering, Job tragically compounded his anguish by doing what he should have learned never to do: He contested God’s wisdom, expressly resenting what the mighty hand of God had brought him. Take time to sense the raw human emotion seething under the words of his lament: I cry out to you, O God, but you do not answer; I stand up, but you merely look at me. You turn on me ruthlessly; with the might of your hand you attack me. You snatch me up and drive me before the wind; you toss me about in the storm. I know you will bring me down to death. (Job 30:20–23 NIV)

What, then, does that statement in Mark 4:33–34 mean: “without a parable He did not speak to them”? That’s a description of Jesus’ public teaching style only during the final year or so of His public ministry. It refers to that intentional change in teaching style that took place about the same time Jesus’ Galilean ministry entered its final phase. As noted earlier, we’ll open chapter 1 by examining the events that provoked Jesus to adopt that style. It was a sudden and striking shift, and a response to hard-hearted, deliberate unbelief and rejection.

Here, then, is the lesson of this first parable: A person’s response to the Word of God is dependent on the condition of that person’s heart. Furthermore, fruit is the only evidence that one has heard the Word rightly. It is not without significance that when Jesus began to unveil the mysteries of the kingdom, this is the first truth He taught. It is a foundational truth, and one that the church today desperately needs to be reminded of. Evangelicals constantly adopt all kinds of bizarre and unbiblical methodologies because they think they can elicit a better response from hard, shallow, or worldly hearts. Some alter the seed, or manufacture synthetic seed. They try to update the message, tone down the offense of the cross, leave the hard or unpopular parts out. Many simply replace the gospel with a totally different message.

The Worldly Hearer The third type of soil, the weedy soil, represents a heart too enthralled or too preoccupied with worldly matters. Jesus explains, “Now the ones that fell among thorns are those who, when they have heard, go out and are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity” (Luke 8:14). Those who fit this category (like the shallow-soil hearers) may seem to respond positively at first. The analogy suggests that there will most likely be some initial sign of receptivity. Seed sown among weeds would germinate. These people, “when they have heard, go out”—meaning, apparently, that they give every sign of pursuing the way of faith. Mark seems to suggest that at first they seem to have every potential to be fruitful, but then at some point afterward, “the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful” (Mark 4:19, emphasis added).

Our Lord said something similar to those who showed a superficial interest in following Him. Discipleship is not a lifestyle to be embarked on heedlessly. He told two parables in Matthew 13 that illustrate the necessity of counting the cost of entering His kingdom. What Is the Kingdom? The kingdom of heaven is a frequent theme in Jesus’ parables. It is the realm over which Christ Himself is the undisputed King of kings and Lord of lords. It is the domain in which His lordship is even now fully operative. In other words, all who truly belong to the kingdom of heaven have formally yielded to Christ’s lordship. To enter the kingdom, therefore, is to enter into eternal life. In short, the kingdom is synonymous with the sphere of salvation—that eternal realm where the redeemed have their true citizenship (Phil. 3:20).

* John Stott, for example, famously wrote, “Emotionally, I find the concept [of hell] intolerable and do not understand how people can live with it without either cauterising their feelings or cracking under the strain.” David L. Edwards and John Stott: Evangelical Essentials: A Liberal-Evangelical Dialogue (London: Hodder & Stoughton, 1988), 313. Stott’s position on the question appeared somewhat ambivalent. He added immediately, “But our emotions are a fluctuating, unreliable guide to truth and must not be exalted to the place of supreme authority in determining it. As a committed Evangelical, my question must be—and is—not what does my heart tell me, but what does God’s word say?” (Ibid.). That’s quite true. But Stott himself did not stop there. He went on to argue for a severely strained interpretation of Scripture that demonstrated his preference for the view that the wicked will ultimately be annihilated.

On an even broader scale, does Jesus’ frequent use of stories constitute a valid argument against the systematic approach to doctrine Christians have historically taken? Do we really even need to analyze Scripture, categorize truth, and attempt to understand biblical doctrine in any kind of logical fashion—or is it okay just to appreciate the stories and embellish them with our own plot twists and real-life endings? In very simple terms: Is Jesus’ own style of teaching actually incompatible with our doctrinal statements, confessions of faith, and systematic approach to theology?
